title: Finite-stalk set-sheaf constructibility from generic lissity on integral affine subschemes
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and $F$ a sheaf of sets on its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Suppose that for every integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] Noetherian affine scheme $S$ and every immersion $g:S\to X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], there is an open subset $W\subset S$ dense in $S$ such that $W\to S\to X$ pulls $F$ back to a finite locally constant sheaf, with finite geometric stalks. Then $F$ has a finite stratification into constructible locally closed subschemes on which its pullbacks are finite locally constant: $F$ is constructible in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. The dense-open hypothesis is stated using iterated set inverse images, as in [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image].

proof.text: Induct on closed subsets using the well-founded order of closed subsets of a Noetherian space. The empty subset has the empty partition. For an irreducible nonempty subset, use the generic lisse stratum theorem and adjoin its partition on the proper closed complement. For a reducible subset, use the reducible partition theorem.

At the whole space, package the finite immersed lisse partition as Stratification.ofNoetherianSpace; the ranges of immersions are locally closed and therefore constructible, and the pullbacks are lisse.

lean.statement:
theorem isConstructibleEtaleSheafOfSets_of_generic_lisse
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X]
    (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (Type (u + 1)))
    (hF : ∀ (S : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral S] [IsNoetherian S] [IsAffine S]
      (g : S ⟶ X) [IsImmersion g],
      ∃ W : S.Opens, Dense (W : Set S) ∧
        IsLisseEtaleSheafOfSets
          ((etaleSetPullback W.ι).obj ((etaleSetPullback g).obj F))) :
    IsConstructibleEtaleSheafOfSets F
